source.title: Effective Does Not Mean Useful: Conditional Functional Substitutability for Redundancy and Scaling in Transformers
source.authors: Jia-Heng Chen; Jia-Xing Li; Yu-Cheng Xiao; Xin-Yong Cai; Jun-Cheng Bu; Lan-Ting Yu; Ting-He Zhang

page_placements.theme: What sets the amount of compensation: training data, objective, pretraining stage, width/scale, training under a lesion

record.tranche_reason: The study removes an attention head and measures how well another head, explicitly gated and scaled as a substitute, restores the model's output. This is a conceptual test of head-level functional recovery, but differs from measuring spontaneous downstream self-repair after ablation.
record.gate_note: Rows cover CFS substitution results for language models: the source head is removed and a candidate substitute is explicitly activated, with recovery measured in predictive-output space. The study does not measure unprompted downstream compensation after ablation. Other reported results, including vision-model experiments, pruning comparisons, and routing results, do not directly measure the language-model self-repair versions here.
record.test_reason: CFS zeroes a source head and then deliberately rescales a chosen other head by a searched α to recover output. This is induced substitution, not compensation arising on its own after ablation. No downstream spontaneous response is measured. Self-repair work (McGrath et al.; Rushing & Nanda) appears only in related work, so the study neither tests nor uses the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that CFS reveals input-conditioned, directional functional redundancy. They also find that Raw Oracle substitutability rises with scale in ViT and Qwen2.5 (weaker in BERT) and that depth scaling gains loss with little substitutability growth. Lower substitutability tracks better loss at fixed capacity, which they offer as a functional account of diminishing returns, and CFS-guided routing beats Taylor importance. They make no claim about spontaneous self-repair.
record.recipe_differences: CFS explicitly removes a source head, activates a candidate substitute with a searched scale, and measures downstream output recovery. It does not measure the original self-repair protocol's naturally arising downstream response to ablation.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported substitutability varies with candidate availability (Raw versus Matched-2), model family and size, scaling axis, and head decomposition. The study also describes input-conditioned variation in substitute identity, but not variation in spontaneous self-repair magnitude.

fits_no_version.finding: After zeroing a head, explicitly rescaling another head (oracle α) recovers 1–44% of the output-KL damage (Raw Oracle). Recovery rises with scale in Qwen2.5 (0.27→0.44) and with width but barely with depth in GPT-2-style models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transformer heads have latent capacity to substitute for an ablated head when deliberately rescaled, and this available substitutability grows with model width and size.

record.code_released: Code, evaluation scripts, and experimental configurations will be released upon acceptance.
record.problems: For the tested language-model results, the reported CFS values are aggregates and no uncertainty estimates are given in the tables. BERT CFS uses a fixed 32-text subset and Qwen2.5 uses 32 contexts. Most importantly, the intervention explicitly adds a substitute head, so it does not establish spontaneous downstream self-repair after ordinary ablation.
record.rows_left_out: No directly relevant language-model CFS results were left out. Vision-only CFS and routing/pruning results were not extracted because they do not directly test the language-model self-repair versions.

untested.parts: No layer ablation or measure of later-layer compensation.
Spontaneous head-level compensation after single-head ablation is not measured. Only explicit, α-scaled substitution is.
No distribution of spontaneous repair or overcorrection.
No backup, copy-suppression, LayerNorm or anti-erasure mechanisms.
Only zero gating is used. There is no mean or resample ablation comparison.
The paper argues importance proxies miss substitutability, but via induced substitutes and ViT pruning. It does not test self-repair biasing ablation scores.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and V3 'supports' labels are withdrawn. The intervention deliberately activates and scales a substitute (gj=α with α searched), which falls under the 'induces the behaviour on purpose' exclusion. Row values match Tables 3–5.

versions.untested_parts: No layer-level ablation or later attention-layer compensation is measured.
No late-MLP downregulation or interaction with earlier-component ablation is measured.

Tests output recovery from explicit substitute-head interventions on language-model predictive distributions, not spontaneous self-repair following ablation; results use limited evaluation contexts rather than a broad full-distribution prompt study.
The study reports input-dependent substitute identities, but does not measure the distribution of spontaneous self-repair amounts or overcorrection after ablation.
Alternative heads are evaluated as explicitly added substitutes, but the study does not identify endogenous backup-head, copy-suppression, LayerNorm, or anti-erasure mechanisms of self-repair.
No comparison of spontaneous self-repair under mean, resample, or zero ablation is made.
The language-model results do not test whether ablation-based importance scores misstate component function because of self-repair.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Section 2 cites self-repair research as related work; the experiments measure a distinct functional-substitution construct.

tranche.reason: CFS measures deliberately induced substitution through candidate selection and searched scaling, rather than spontaneous compensation after ablation. It tests no listed claim version.

source_check.notes: All four BERT values and the definition-based zero baseline are supported. Their cannot_determine states correctly distinguish induced substitution from the catalog's self-repair claims.

statements.problem: The rounded 1–44% range needs a language-model qualifier: ViT reaches 60.34%. The small depth-related increase specifically describes D12→D18; the full depth trajectory is nonmonotonic.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Language-model CFS substitution results across BERT, Qwen2.5, and controlled GPT-2-style settings
reader_labels.reason: All reported Raw Oracle and Matched-2 recovery values are above the zero-recovery reference, indicating partial output recovery when an explicitly selected substitute head is activated (r1–r32).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Interpretation of all reported language-model CFS results as self-repair
reader_labels.reason: The recovery is produced by an explicit source-removal plus substitute-head intervention, not by measuring spontaneous changes in later components after ablation; BERT Tiny also has low reported recovery (r1–r2).
